s1.syndrome_frame: A middle-aged woman with a long-standing breast lump and migratory discomfort in the right axilla and upper-outer quadrant
salient_findings: Mobile lump in the right breast
Migratory discomfort and pain in the right axilla and upper-outer quadrant
Multiple hypoechoic masses with varying sizes and locations in the right breast on ultrasonography
key_facts: 58-year-old woman
3-year history of a right-breast lump
No family history of breast cancer
Menopausal for 5 years
Denied eating frogs or snakes
Recalled drinking impure water
Mobile lump palpated in the right breast
Migratory discomfort and pain in the right axilla and upper-outer quadrant
Breast ultrasonography revealed multiple hypoechoic masses
No obvious blood-flow signals detected within the lesions on color Doppler flow imaging

Multiple hypoechoic masses with varying sizes and locations in the right breast on ultrasonography

shortlist.label: Invasive ductal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Most common type of breast cancer, consistent with patient's age and presentation

shortlist.label: Fibroadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign tumor that can present as a mobile lump, consistent with patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Phyllodes tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Rare tumor that can present as a lump, consistent with patient's symptoms and ultrasonography findings

shortlist.label: Ductal carcinoma in situ
shortlist.why_kept: Pre-invasive cancer that can present as a lump, consistent with patient's symptoms and ultrasonography findings

shortlist.label: Tubular carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Type of invasive cancer that can present as a hypoechoic mass, consistent with patient's ultrasonography findings

raw.rationale: The presence of multiple hypoechoic masses with well-delineated contours and no obvious blood-flow signals on color Doppler flow imaging, along with the patient's age and the mobile nature of the lump, are more consistent with fibroadenoma, a common benign breast tumor.

rejected.label: Invasive ductal carcinoma
rejected.why: The lack of family history, absence of blood-flow signals, and the description of the masses are less typical for invasive ductal carcinoma

rejected.label: Phyllodes tumor
rejected.why: Phyllodes tumors are less common and often present with more rapid growth and larger size at diagnosis

rejected.label: Ductal carcinoma in situ
rejected.why: DCIS typically does not form palpable masses and is often detected by mammography as microcalcifications

rejected.label: Tubular carcinoma
rejected.why: Tubular carcinoma is a subtype of invasive ductal carcinoma and would be expected to have more suspicious features on imaging, such as irregular margins or increased vascularity
